source.title: Beyond Refusal Patterns: Safe-Role Internalization for Robust and Generalizable LLM Safety Alignment
source.authors: Jin-Hao Pang; Jitai Hao; Qiang Huang; Zhao-Chun Ren; Jun Yu

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some figures and one dataset-composition chart have garbled OCR, but the relevant prefilling-attack results are readable in Table 5 and its accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies affirmative-prefix prefilling attacks and measures harmful-query ASR after different fine-tuning approaches. It tests the bypass behavior with a behavioral outcome, but does not measure per-token KL divergence.
record.gate_note: The study reports Table 5 outcomes for prefilling attacks on three benchmarks and their reported average. SSRFT and SFT are the study's own training methods, so the rows record their measured response to prefilling; the claims that existing safety alignment generally changes early tokens are background claims or citations, not this study's measurements. Benign instruction data appears in a mixed SFT baseline, so its independent effect is not isolated.
record.test_reason: The paper applies Qi et al.'s affirmative-prefix prefilling attack to refusal-SFT models, testing V4. It also proposes SSRFT, a training method meant to keep safety past the opening tokens, and measures how well it holds under prefilling, testing V7. Everything else is untested: no per-token KL, no harmful or benign-only fine-tuning of an aligned model, no parameter localisation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that refusal-centric SFT shows shallow alignment and degrades sharply under prefilling. SSRFT, by internalising a safe role, is substantially more robust than matched SFT on most Base models and on Qwen3-4B-Instruct, with gains depending on model capability and existing alignment. The comparison is always against SFT, and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct is a counterexample where SSRFT is worse.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning on role-oriented Safe-Role Question-Answer data, compared with a standard SFT baseline; the prefilling intervention follows the cited affirmative-prefix setup. This is not a reproduction of the original harmful-example fine-tuning or tokenwise-KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefilling effects vary by model, training method, and prompt set; the study also reports differences between Base and Instruct models.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASR results. The prefilling test uses one affirmative prefix and does not test suffixes or decoding changes. The proposed role-internalization explanation is not directly verified with token-position measurements.

untested.parts: No harmful-example fine-tuning of an aligned model.
The SFT baseline mixes benign data with refusal pairs; no benign-only fine-tuning of an aligned model.
No per-token KL or position-wise measurement.
Only one affirmative prefix; no suffixes or decoding attacks.
The refusal-pattern account is asserted, not tested.
No measurement that safety is spread across positions; robustness only to one fixed prefix; no fine-tuning attacks.

missing.what: SSRFT prefilling rows for Gemma2-2B (average 1.09→23.28), Llama3.1-8B (0.92→16.54), LRC-4B (0.16→4.98) and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct (0.16→28.58), with per-benchmark values
Correct Qwen3-4B-Instruct original row (average 1.03→2.03) and SFT row (0.00→6.74)
Non-expanded SFT/SSRFT prefilling results; Non-Expanded SSRFT on Qwen2.5-3B-Ins (23.35 vs SFT 15.63)
LRC-4B comparison: PKU-SafeRLHF prefilled ASR 52.44, prompt role-play 16.71, SSRFT 4.98

record.verdict_notes: The record's core error: Table 5 has three rows per model (original, SFT, SSRFT). The reader labelled original as SFT and SFT as SSRFT for Gemma, Llama, LRC and Qwen2.5-3B-Ins. For Qwen2.5-3B it read original and SSRFT, and the Qwen3-4B-Ins block is garbled. Original Base models have no safety training, so they bear on no version. No uncertainty estimates; single judge (MD-Judge); single fixed prefix.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment fine-tunes an already safety-trained model on a small set of harmful examples to test whether it begins complying.

The SFT baseline mixes benign instruction conversations with jailbreak-refusal pairs; the study does not isolate the effect of benign-only or carefully selected benign-only fine-tuning on harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL divergence or other response-position distribution measurement is reported.
Tests affirmative-prefix prefilling only. It does not test adversarial suffixes or decoding changes.
No localization or ablation of safety in a small set of weights or ranks.
The paper proposes an account contrasting refusal-oriented supervision and role internalization, but does not directly identify the cause of token-position shallowness.

SSRFT is evaluated as a training approach for robustness to prefilling, but the study does not directly measure whether safety is distributed across response positions or establish token-depth changes.

reader_labels.label: supports
